newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong Catholic bishop-designate consecrated.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong Catholic bishop-designate consecrated.

text.p: The Roman Catholic Church consecrated a new bishop for Hong Kong on Monday in a mass attended by bishops from Taiwan and other Asian nations, but not by Vatican representatives.

The Hong Kong diocese urged followers to regard the ceremony, attended by a congregation of about 1,300 in Hong Kong's Roman Catholic Cathedral, as a religious occasion and said it should not be linked to politics.
Shanghai-born Monsignor Joseph Zen, 64, became Coadjudicator Bishop, successor designate to Hong Kong's Cardinal Joseph Wu.
Monsignor John Tong became Auxiliary Bishop of Hong Kong in a ceremony conducted by Wu. It was not clear exactly when Zen and Tong would take up their new duties.
"There is a seat empty (in China) which should be filled by a Bishop," Zen said.
"We hope in the future there may be a normalisation of the situation of the church so we may join together," Zen said, referring to the division between Roman Catholics in China and Hong Kong.

A church spokeswoman rejected speculation that the two appointments signalled the imminent departure of Wu and dismissed press reports he would step down with the handover of Hong Kong to China at midnight on June 30, 1997.
She said that Wu, 71, had not reached the retirement age of 75, and the appointments were "helpful" to ensuring a smooth transition.
The Vatican has diplomatic relations with Taiwan but not with China, which resumes sovereignty over the British colony of Hong Kong next year.

Beijing does not recognise the ultimate authority of the Vatican in religious affairs and insists that Chinese Catholics worshipping openly do so under the auspices of the country's state-sponsored Catholic Patriotic Association.
China and Britain have been at loggerheads over democratic reforms introduced into Hong Kong and has subjected Patten, who sponsored them, to sharp criticism.
Wu became the first Hong Kong priest to be elevated to Cardinal. He was consecrated before Pope Paul II at the Vatican in 1988. Some 270,000 Roman Catholics live in Hong Kong, the diocese said.
The ceremony, which was also attended by the Governor Chris Patten, who is a Roman Catholic, was beamed by closed-circuit television to some 200 to 300 followers outside.
